title: 3D time-lapse microscopy paired with endpoint lineage analysis in mouse blastocysts
protocol: Euthanize pregnant females at E3.5 according to approved institutional animal care and use committee protocol.
Place mouse onto absorbent pad in dissection area in a supine position (abdomen facing up).
Spray the animal with 70% ethanol.
Make a transverse incision in the skin and peritoneum crossing the midline of the animal.
Dissect the uterus by removing adipose tissue and viscera.
Outline the visible uterus and make cuts as indicated to dissect uterine horns.
Flush embryos from the uterine horns using PBS.
Collect flushed embryos for the experiment.
Using forceps, move skin, fatty tissue, and intestines to reveal the uterus.
Dissect the uterus by cutting just below the cervix and between the oviduct and ovaries.
Transfer dissected uterus to a 60-mm dish with PBS.
Cut each uterine horn at the uterotubal junction (UTJ) and near where it meets the cervix.
Add ~300 μL warm M2 to a 35-mm dish.
Place one uterine horn from the PBS into the drop of M2.
Fill a 1 mL syringe with warm M2.
Insert needle tip into the uterine horn near where the UTJ cut was made.
Gently flush the uterine horn with 0.5 mL M2.
Remove and dispose of tissue that was flushed with media.
Repeat flushing step with the second uterine horn.
Allow approximately 1 min for embryos to settle at the bottom of the dish.
Scan the plate for embryos using a dissection microscope.
Transfer embryos from M2 media into one drop of KSOM in the embryo culture dish.
Wash embryos by sequentially passing them through each of the KSOM drops.
Optionally, remove zona pellucida (ZP) by acid wash.
Place the culture dish containing embryos into a 37°C 5% CO2 incubator.
Turn on microscope, camera, light source, and stage incubator for embryo imaging.
Prepare the embryo imaging plate by arranging drops of ~0.2 μL KSOM onto the imaging plate.
Cover the KSOM drops with mineral oil to prevent evaporation.
Mix 15 mM sterile HCl to reconstitute human recombinant leptin.
Cover the drops with mineral oil for imaging.
Place the plate in a 37°C 5% CO2 incubator for at least 30 min.
Transfer one embryo to each drop of the imaging plate for mounting.
Position embryos such that the embryonic-abembryonic axis runs parallel to the plane of the coverslip.
Set imaging plate onto the microscope stage.
Perform imaging according to biosensors/fluorescent reporters used in experiment.
Optimize conditions based on experimental parameters and individual microscope assemblies.
Use exposure time of 200-250 ms for imaging.
Set laser power at 22%-25% of maximum during imaging.
Capture images with Z-stacks at 5 μm steps.
Image embryos every 15 minutes.
Continue to step 20, 1 hour before the end of the imaging interval.
Prepare a 96-well round bottom plate for immunofluorescence.
Microwave 10 mL molecular biology-grade water with 1% agar and 0.9% NaCl until dissolved.
Pipette 50 μL of coating solution into each well of a 96-well round bottom plate.
Gently tap the plate on the bench top to settle the solution in all wells.
Cover the plate with a lid or aluminum foil.
Store the plate in a refrigerator at 4°C.
Use the prepared plate within 24 hours.
Retrieve embryos for immunofluorescence staining.
Thaw 1 mL of 4% formaldehyde in PBS.
Label the coated 96-well round bottom plate according to Table 1.
Pipette 100 μL of 4% formaldehyde into column 1 of the labeled plate.
Pipette 100 μL of PBX into column 2 of the labeled plate.
Bring the imaging plate and immunofluorescence plate to the dissection microscope immediately after imaging.
Transfer embryos from the imaging plate into column 1 of the immunofluorescence plate containing 4% formaldehyde at a ratio of one embryo per well.
Incubate embryos for 10 min at 20°C–25°C.
Wash embryos once by passing them into PBX.
Transfer fixed embryos to a well with 4% BSA in PBS and cover with mineral oil to prevent evaporation.
Incubate embryos in permeabilization buffer for 5 min at 20°C–25°C.
Wash embryos once in PBX.
Block embryos 1 h at 20°C–25°C.
Incubate embryos in primary antibody diluted in blocking buffer at least 16 h at 4°C.
Cover wells containing primary antibody with mineral oil to prevent evaporation and cover plate with lid or aluminum foil.
Fill columns 7–11 with solutions according to Table 1 on the following day.
Wash embryos three times in PBX.
Block embryos 1 h at 20°C–25°C.
Incubate embryos in secondary antibody diluted in blocking buffer for 60–90 min at 20°C–25°C.
Cover wells with mineral oil and protect from light.
Wash embryos twice in PBX.
Leave embryos in PBX after the last wash.
Prepare an imaging plate using PBS as the mounting medium.
Wash embryos once in PBS.
Transfer embryos to the imaging plate carefully.
Arrange embryos on the imaging plate in the same position and orientation they were in for live imaging.
Load nuclear marker images representing the last frame of the time-lapse imaging and fixed images of each embryo using an image processing program like Fiji.
Examine both image stacks closely for each embryo by eye.
Determine if the datasets can be aligned based on morphological and cytological features in the live and fixed image stacks.
Record which embryos failed to align.
Take the imaging plate back to the dissection microscope.
Gently reposition any embryos that could not be aligned using a mouth pipette.
Rotate the blastocysts along the embryonic-abembryonic axis if necessary.
Re-image the embryos manipulated previously.
Check alignment and repeat steps as necessary until images suitable for analysis are obtained.
Keep the total number of times any embryo is imaged to three or fewer.
Proceed with analysis of time-lapse and fixed imaging data after obtaining aligned images.
Load time-lapse and immunofluorescence image data in Fiji as stacks.
Perform image translation or rotation using the nuclear marker channel in each stack to identify corresponding cells in each dataset.
Crop the images if it is helpful for identification.
Duplicate the nuclear marker channel of the immunofluorescence image stack.
Use the multi-point tool to give all cells that will be analyzed a number on the duplicate nuclear marker stack.
Select “Analyze -> Set Measurements…” in the Fiji menu to preset the parameters for recording measurements.
Analyze cell 1 on the time-lapse stack starting from the last frame.
Identify the starting position of the cell working backwards through frames.
Measure independent intensities for the nucleus and cytoplasm using ERK-KTR.
Draw regions of interest around the nucleus and cytoplasm for each time point.
Use the nuclear marker signal to identify the nucleus and cytoplasm.
Make measurements in the plane where the nucleus has the greatest diameter.
Do not exclude nucleolar areas in the region of interest.
Measure a narrow region immediately bordering the nucleus to avoid neighboring cells.
Continue analyzing the remaining cells in the time-lapse stack.
Save the measurements in preferred spreadsheet software.
Measure nuclear intensities of lineage markers stained for in immunofluorescence protocol.
Draw nuclear regions of interest for measuring intensity.
Measure cells according to the same numbering convention as previously specified.
Save the immunofluorescence data analysis.
Proceed with analyzing remaining embryos from the experiment.
